svg.title: The agreement cases pin the recorded copy, not the caller's citation
svg.desc: Before: the row's gate_check.log_path is the path the caller cited, which a worker's scratch log loses to the reaper. After: promotion copies the cited log into the run directory and the row cites that copy, so four agreement cases assert the path lies inside the run directory and its bytes equal the cited source. The unreadable-citation case is left alone, because an absent citation is handed on unchanged.
svg.text: Promotion redirects the row's citation to a copy inside the run directory; the agreement cases assert both halves of that claim.
Before the copy step: the row cited where the log lay
--gate-log-path /tmp/w/gate.log
gate_check.log_path = "/tmp/w/gate.log"
/tmp reaped,
worktree removed
A path that was true only when it was written: every check on the row passes, and the evidence is gone.
After: the row cites a copy the run directory keeps
cited /tmp/w/gate.log
copy
<run-dir>/gate.log
gate_check.log_path = "<run-dir>/gate.log"
The assertion is the pair: citation.parent == run_dir(run_id), and citation's bytes == the cited source's bytes.
Either half alone is satisfiable without the evidence surviving with it.
Retargeted to the recorded copy (4 cases)
agreeing exit status · executed exit beside a quote
fixture diagnostic beside a summary · log and command agree
Left unmodified (1 case)
a citation this machine cannot read is handed on unchanged,
so an absent log still cannot turn a passing gate into a refusal.
